valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E: FY2027 underlying EPS viewed at the 12-month target date (Nov 2027), times a justified P/E, in USD per ADS. ADR ratio: one UL ADS represents one Unilever PLC ordinary share (1:1, per the depositary programme), so per-share values carry over without scaling. Unilever reports in EUR; EUR/USD 1.1127 (Banca d'Italia reference rate, 11 Nov 2026, the nearest sourced date; the 13 Nov rate could not be retrieved) converts EPS and dividend. Anchor: FY2025 underlying EPS EUR 3.08 (+0.7%, continuing operations after the Magnum ice cream demerger). Q3 2026 underlying sales growth 5.2% (volume +2.9%, price +2.3%); guidance raised to at least 3% FY2026 volume growth, USG within 4-6%, modest underlying operating margin improvement from 20.0%; EUR 1.5bn buyback from Q2 2026. FY2026E EPS EUR 3.15 and FY2027E EPS EUR 3.35 are my own assumptions (no company EPS guidance; no sourced consensus EPS).

bear.driver: Commodity cost inflation and weak developed-market Foods volumes squeeze margin; price-led growth fades and the multiple de-rates.

base.driver: USG about 4-5%, modest margin gain and buybacks give roughly 6% EPS growth on FY2026E; FX roughly neutral.

bull.driver: Volume-led growth in emerging markets and Home Care/Personal Care sustains the top of the 4-6% range with margin expansion.

valuation.implied_by_close: At base EPS of $3.73 the $66.21 close implies 17.8x. The analyst-weighted target of $76 implies 20.4x, or about $4.22 of EPS (EUR 3.79) at 18x.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $3.73 (5.6 pp of the close); EUR 0.10 of FY2027 EPS moves it by $2.00 (3.0 pp).
valuation.watch_metric: Underlying sales growth split between volume and price (Q3: 5.2%, volume +2.9%) and underlying operating margin versus 20.0% in 2025.
valuation.next_disclosure: FY2026 results with 2027 outlook, expected February 2027 (date not confirmed; FY2025 was released 12 Feb 2026).

analyst_notes: Two named US-listing calls were sourced: TD Cowen's Robert Moskow (target 67 to 76) and BofA's Nicolas Ceron (72 to 76), both Buy after Q2 results on 29 Jul 2026; both pre-date the Q3 update of 28 Oct and neither has a documented 12-month horizon, so they stay out of the weighted target. Firm-only London-line calls (Jefferies Underperform GBX 4,000, Berenberg Underperform GBX 4,000, Deutsche Bank Hold GBX 5,150, Bernstein Buy GBX 5,800) have no named analyst. The $76 targets imply about EPS $4.22 at 18x versus my $3.73, a roughly 13% EPS gap or 2.4 turns of multiple; MarketBeat shows a Hold consensus near $65.55.
